title: Humayun's garden tomb, Delhi
alt: Red sandstone mausoleum with a pale dome, arched recesses, palms and lawn
caption: The mausoleum commemorates Humayun after his death; the surviving garden and masonry have undergone conservation. Compare the elevated tomb with its garden setting, rather than treating this as an image of his 1555 restoration. Modern photograph: 2021-08-05 17:15:57. Reproduced without further cropping.

title: Panch Mahal at Fatehpur Sikri
alt: Five diminishing storeys of an open red sandstone pavilion supported by columns
caption: A surviving pavilion in Akbar's planned capital. Its open columned storeys show court architecture; they do not identify the location or participants of a particular religious debate. Modern photograph: 2009-12-04. Reproduced without further cropping.

title: Taj Mahal, Agra
alt: White marble mausoleum and four minarets beyond a garden and reflecting channel
caption: The central mausoleum and its minarets belong to Shah Jahan's funerary complex for Mumtaz Mahal. The photograph does not show the entire riverfront, mosque, guest house or construction sequence. Modern photograph: 6 March 2004 (according to Exif data). Reproduced without further cropping.
credit: Dhirad, picture edited by J. A. Knudsen / Wikimedia Commons

title: Arched entrance passage at the Red Fort
alt: Successive pointed red sandstone arches opening into a shaded passage with visitors and shops
caption: The palace-fort anchors Shah Jahan's new capital. The surviving entrance includes later alterations; the modern flag and visitors belong to the photograph, not seventeenth-century court life. Modern photograph: 2021-10-08 12:30:10. Reproduced without further cropping.

title: Basilica of Bom Jesus, Old Goa
alt: Ornamented stone church facade with a central doorway and tall rectangular windows
caption: A later monument of Portuguese Goa, built long after the conquest of 1510. This church illustrates the colonial religious landscape, not the landing, conquest or the first printing press. Modern photograph: 2024-08-11 10:34:36. Reproduced without further cropping.

title: Stone chariot at the Vittala temple, Hampi
alt: Carved stone chariot shrine with wheels and elephant sculptures in a temple courtyard
caption: A surviving sacred monument within the Vijayanagara landscape. This modern photograph is not evidence of how the battle of Talikota unfolded or a record of destruction in 1565. The complex developed in multiple phases. Modern photograph: 2016-09-10 15:19:25. Reproduced without further cropping.

title: Gol Gumbaz, Bijapur
alt: Large domed mausoleum flanked by corner towers beyond a garden approach
caption: The seventeenth-century mausoleum of Muhammad Adil Shah gives a specific Bijapur example within the wider Deccan court story. It is not a building from the opening date of every sultanate. Modern photograph: 2025-10-12 20:09:29. Reproduced without further cropping.

title: Surviving architecture at Golconda
alt: Weathered plaster and stone walls with pointed arched niches inside Golconda Fort
caption: The fort preserves several building phases and subsequent conservation. Read it as the material setting of Qutb Shahi power; a modern view cannot reconstruct the Mughal siege deployments of 1687. Modern photograph: 13 October 2025 (according to Exif data). Reproduced without further cropping.

title: Surviving masonry at Raigad
alt: Three arched openings in a ruined stone wall overlooking a misty hill landscape
caption: Raigad connects the coronation story to its hill-fort setting. This view of surviving rooms does not identify the coronation platform or reproduce the ceremony of 1674. Modern photograph: 2009-09-25 12:06. Reproduced without further cropping.

title: Sindhudurg sea-facing walls
alt: Stone fort walls following a rocky shore beside the sea
caption: Compare this coastal fortification with Raigad's hill setting. The different terrain helps explain defensive choices; the photograph alone cannot establish garrison size or the range of naval control. Modern photograph: 2012-12-26. Reproduced without further cropping.

title: Masonry instruments at Jantar Mantar, Jaipur
alt: Triangular masonry structure beside curved graduated surfaces at Jaipur observatory
caption: These fixed structures supported naked-eye astronomical observation. They are instruments, not merely monumental sculpture. A working explanation needs an identified instrument, orientation and scale; the photograph is not a measured drawing. Modern photograph: 2019-12-18 09:06:46. Reproduced without further cropping.

title: Decorated portal in Jaipur City Palace
alt: Green painted scalloped arch framing a gold-coloured door in Jaipur City Palace
caption: A detail of the surviving palace complex, which accumulated additions after Jaipur's foundation in 1727. Do not date this particular decoration to the founding year or treat it as a city-plan view. Modern photograph: 2019-12-18 10:00:01. Reproduced without further cropping.

title: Sher Shah Suri's tomb at Sasaram
alt: Domed stone mausoleum on a platform in a lake, approached by a causeway
caption: The Sur ruler's mausoleum supplies architectural context for the dynasty that displaced Humayun. It is not an image of Humayun's exile, restoration, or a specimen of Sher Shah's currency. Modern photograph: Taken on 10 June 2012, 16:51:16. Reproduced without further cropping.

title: Tomb of Itimad-ud-Daulah, Agra
alt: Pale marble mausoleum with four corner towers beyond a garden channel
caption: Nur Jahan's patronage of her father's tomb provides material evidence of elite women's architectural commissions. It does not replace a dated coin, seal or document for studying her political authority. Modern photograph: 2024-12-16 15:27:55. Reproduced without further cropping.

title: Shaniwar Wada, Pune
alt: Large closed gateway between rounded stone bastions at Shaniwar Wada
caption: The Peshwa residence gives a place-based context for eighteenth-century Maratha power. Surviving gateways and ruins are not a map of direct rule, tribute or campaigns, and the complex changed after this timeline window. Modern photograph: 2021-12-13. Reproduced without further cropping.

title: Courtyard at Padmanabhapuram Palace
alt: Grass courtyard and trees surrounded by white walls and sloping tiled roofs
caption: The former Travancore capital provides a courtly context for Marthanda Varma's reign. The palace has multiple building phases; this is neither the battlefield at Colachel nor a depiction of the Dutch surrender. Modern photograph: 2024-03-24 11:26:53. Reproduced without further cropping.

title: Portrait of Emperor Jahangir
alt: Small profile portrait of Jahangir framed by calligraphy and floral album borders
caption: ca. 1615–20. Ink, opaque watercolor, and gold on paper. Met 13.228.47. A portrait dated around 1615-20, within Jahangir's reign. Courtly representation is not an unmediated record of everyday government. Reproduced without cropping.

title: Prince Aurangzeb
alt: Bust portrait of Prince Aurangzeb in profile wearing a jewelled turban and floral robe
caption: ca. 1653–55. Opaque watercolor and gold on cloth. Met 2022.182. A princely portrait dated around 1653-55, before the succession war and Aurangzeb's accession. It cannot illustrate a particular battle or alliance. Reproduced without cropping.

title: Equestrian Portrait of Aurangzeb
alt: Aurangzeb riding a dark horse and holding a long spear within an ornamental border
caption: 17th century. Opaque watercolor on paper. Met 25.138.1. The catalogue dates this equestrian portrait to the seventeenth century. Royal imagery does not establish the effects of individual policies. Reproduced without cropping.
credit: The Metropolitan Museum of Art; Rogers Fund, 1925

title: Palampore
alt: Cotton hanging with a branching flowering tree, birds, animals and a red floral border
caption: first quarter of the 18th century. Cotton (painted resist and mordant, dyed). Met 2010.337. An early eighteenth-century Coromandel palampore made for the Sri Lankan market. Indian Ocean textile demand extended beyond European companies; this object is not proof of a particular Company shipment. Reproduced without cropping.

title: Darbar Sahib at Kartarpur today
alt: White domed gurdwara in a broad paved courtyard with distant visitors
caption: A modern view of the sacred site associated with Guru Nanak's final community. The present complex is not a sixteenth-century building. Kartarpur lies in present-day Pakistan; it appears here for its direct place in the history of Punjab and Sikh traditions, not as a claim about modern borders. Photograph: 2021-02-14 14:34:40. Reproduced without further cropping.

title: Ahmadnagar Fort entrance
alt: Stone fort walls and a recessed entrance beyond an overgrown moat
caption: A modern photograph of the surviving fort entrance. It provides the setting for Chand Bibi's defence, not the fort's exact 1595 appearance or an eyewitness depiction of the siege. Photograph: 2017-10-14 12:52:29. Reproduced without further cropping.

title: Memorial near the Plassey battlefield
alt: Tall pale obelisk on a stone base bearing a Battle Field of Plassey inscription
caption: A later commemorative monument photographed in 2019. A memorial marks how a battle is remembered; it is not a contemporary battle plan or evidence for troop numbers and casualties. Photograph: 2019-01-17 09:51:05. Reproduced without further cropping.

title: The Diwani grant, imagined by Benjamin West c. 1818
alt: Later oil painting of Shah Alam seated beneath a canopy presenting a scroll to Clive among attendants
caption: British Library Foster 29, a later version commissioned around 1818 of West's earlier painting. It represents the 1765 grant from a subsequent British imperial perspective. It is not an eyewitness image or a facsimile of the grant itself. Reproduced without further cropping.

title: Shivaji: a late seventeenth-century album portrait
alt: Profile portrait of Shivaji in a patterned white robe and turban, holding a sword hilt
caption: British Museum 1974,0617,0.11.12; the linked record dates the painting to 1680-1687. This is later than the coronation of 1674 and should not be read as a depiction of that ceremony. Reproduced without further cropping.

title: Portrait of Malik Ambar attributed to Hashim
alt: Malik Ambar standing in profile in a white robe and turban with a red staff
caption: An early seventeenth-century portrait associated with Hashim, reproduced from the V&A collection through Commons. Published captions give dates around the early 1620s. The portrait presents an individual statesman; it is not a visual record of his whole army or a literal reconstruction of a campaign. Reproduced without further cropping.
credit: Hashim (made) / Wikimedia Commons / Victoria and Albert Museum

title: Krishna temple: rear of the shrine, Hampi
alt: Carved horizontal stone panels and niches along the back of the Krishna temple shrine
caption: The temple belongs to Krishnadevaraya's patronage. Modern descriptions often use 1513, while an epigraphic discussion published by Government Museum Chennai distinguishes the campaign from installation in 1515. Keep those dates separate rather than dating every surviving stone to one year. Photograph: 2023-01-26 12:17:33. Reproduced without further cropping.

title: Stepped tank near the Krishna temple, Hampi
alt: Water tank with broad stone steps and surrounding colonnades reflected in the water
caption: A modern view of the stepped tank associated with the Krishna temple landscape. It supports comparison of sacred architecture and water management, not a measured reconstruction of the entire capital. Photograph: 2012-12-20 07:14:15. Reproduced without further cropping.
